destination.name: Port Moresby
destination.tagline: A Coral Sea gateway city where most trips to Papua New Guinea begin.
destination.description: Port Moresby is the capital and largest city of Papua New Guinea, on the Coral Sea at the south-western end of the Papuan Peninsula. Almost all visitors to the country pass through it, but it has few attractions and is mostly a stop on the way to other regions. Those who stay can see the National Museum and Art Gallery, Port Moresby Nature Park with its birds of paradise and cassowaries, and Parliament Haus. At about 899 mm of rain a year it is the driest place in New Guinea, and the original Motu-Koitabu settlement of Hanuabada is still on the harbour.

goodToKnow.title: Arrange every ride
goodToKnow.detail: The city is spread out and walking between places is not advised. Book transfers through your hotel, or agree a taxi fare before setting off (taxis rarely use meters) and give the hotel the driver's name and number.

goodToKnow.title: Crime is a real issue
goodToKnow.detail: Carjackings and muggings are common and foreigners are sometimes targeted, so do not travel at night. Most hotels are guarded compounds and you will probably spend evenings in yours, so choose one with a restaurant; expect high prices.

goodToKnow.title: Visa and arrival
goodToKnow.detail: Everyone needs a visa; many nationalities get 60 days on arrival at Jacksons Airport, but not for stays under 8 hours, so transit passengers cannot leave the terminal. Tell your hotel your arrival time and whether you land at the international or domestic terminal.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: The drier months, {months}, see the least rain; the wet season runs from about December to May.
